headline: ASUS' first gaming soundbar, ROG Gjallar, is now available in the US for $600
summary: The ASUS ROG Gjallar, priced at $600, is designed for multiplayer gaming, offering 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos audio and headset-free communication with integrated noise-cancelling microphones.
details: ASUS has launched its first gaming soundbar, the ROG Gjallar, in the US for $600. Designed with multiplayer gaming in mind, it features an audio control hub with integrated microphones for headset-free communication.

The soundbar boasts 5.1.2-channel speaker configuration for immersive three-dimensional Dolby Atmos audio. It includes a wireless 6.5-inch 65W subwoofer with a dedicated 5GHz connection to prevent lags.

The audio control hub also has an LCD display for volume, playback, input selection, and EQ profiles. ASUS states its technology filters teammate voices and in-game audio while suppressing background noise for clear communication.

Connectivity options include USB-C, HDMI 2.1 with eARC, optical, 3.5mm AUX, and Bluetooth 5.3. It's compatible with gaming PCs, Macs, mobile devices, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and TVs, plus two USB Type-A ports for accessories.
The ROG Gjallar is listed on Best Buy and ASUS' US website. While currently showing as sold out or awaiting stock, users can sign up for 'Notify Me' alerts on ASUS' site for availability updates.

headline_marked: [[Ambient Context]] creates screen memory from text, not screenshots, for your LLM
headline: Ambient Context creates screen memory from text, not screenshots, for your LLM
summary: This macOS menu bar app records focused window text to a daily Markdown file, enabling your LLM to recall past work, build project memory, or even write stand-ups.
details: Ambient Context is a new macOS menu bar application designed to create a textual record of your daily work. It reads the text from your currently focused window every few seconds using the macOS accessibility tree and appends it to a plain Markdown file, with one file generated per day.

This daily record serves as a memory for your large language models (LLMs) or AI agents. You can point tools like Claude Code at this folder to answer questions like "what did I work on Tuesday?", build project-specific knowledge, or even automate the creation of daily stand-up reports.

The app is currently in early development and is unsigned, meaning there is no notarized download available yet as Apple Developer enrollment is in progress. For now, users need to build the application themselves from the source code, a process that reportedly takes about two minutes.

Once built, the app resides in your Applications folder. Its functionality is controlled via a menu bar icon: an open eye indicates recording, while a closed eye means it's paused. Right-clicking the icon provides quick access to today's file, the capture folder, and settings.

Privacy and security are key design considerations. Ambient Context only reads the focused window, never background windows, other displays, or minimized windows, and it pauses when the screen is locked. It explicitly excludes password managers and private browsing, skips secure input fields, and pattern-scrubs secrets before writing to disk. All data is stored locally as plaintext, and the capture folder itself is excluded from observation to prevent self-capture.
